newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures finish narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures finish narrowly mixed.

text.p: U.S. debt futures finished narrowly mixed, as September T-bonds gravitated to the upside on late local short-covering, traders and analysts said.
"This market trades like it wants to go higher," one T-bond futures analyst said. "Our downtrades last for about an hour."

September T-bonds were slightly lower for most of the day, but traders were impressed with the market's ability to sustain its recovery off the daily low of 113-07/32. Some locals remained short, but were forced to cover positions once September T-bonds climbed above 113-28/32, traders said.
Short-term resistance is now at 114-01/32, traders said.

Volume was extremely light in afternoon trade in both the T-bond and Eurodollar pits, traders said. They said Tuesday's volume was on par with Monday's official bond futures volume of 146,755 contracts.
Eurodollar volume was estimated at 350,000, a trader said.

Good two-way flows were reported in the T-bond futures pit immediately after U.S. June retail sales data were released. Floor analysts said talk circulated that foreign central banks and hedge funds were good buyers during the recovery.

Retail sales rose 0.5 percent, above average trade estimates for a 0.2 percent gain. However, the sales figure was offset by a smaller than expected rise in sales excluding cars, coupled with downward-revised data for May, they said.
The U.S. weekly Redbook retail sales index fell 0.2 percent.

Traders are looking for subdued price pressures in the U.S. June consumer price index, which will be released on Wednesday at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT. CPI is seen rising 0.2 percent overall and in the core rate.
At the end of pit trade, September T-bonds and December Eurodollars were unchanged at 113-30/32 and 94.04, respectively.
In other contracts, the September 10-year T-note also closed steady at 109-14/32, and munibonds were up 04/32 at 119-16/32. ((Chicago Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
